Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the intro and demo earlier today — appreciate the clear overview. As promised, here are the key performance targets we discussed so our infra team can validate: 

- Latency SLO (p95): 150ms for US production queries (text-gen, avg prompt ~250 tokens)
- EU target: p95 <= 200ms (data residency requirement for EU customers)
- APAC target: p95 <= 300ms (initial)
- Throughput: baseline 120 req/s, expected peak bursts to 350 req/s (sustained for short windows)
- Concurrency: 40 concurrent live streams (we use streaming over websockets for UI)
- Streaming: chunked streaming with very low tail latency (goal: first-byte <= 80ms)

We also have a couple of constraints:
1) EU data must be processed and stored within EU regions only — this may require a private deployment or VPC option.
2) We will need audit logs and retention for 12 months.

Can Aditya or you confirm whether Redwood can meet these SLOs with a multi-region routing setup and what operational mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private) you recommend? Also please share any template SLO worksheet so we can fill in exact traffic profile details.

Cheers,
Alex

Hi Alex — quick technical readout after reviewing the targets and typical prompt sizes (250 tokens avg):

1) Feasibility (hosted):
- US: p95 150ms is achievable for single-turn text-gen on our optimized serving runtime when pinned to a dedicated pool with continuous batching disabled for lowest tail latency.
- EU: 200ms p95 is achievable from EU regions if traffic terminates in EU and you use regional routing.
- APAC: 300ms p95 is reasonable from APAC regions on cloud-hosted infra (may need slightly larger instance types for sustained bursts).

2) Deployment recommendation:
- For EU data residency + 12mo audit logs: Private (VPC) or Dedicated in EU will be simplest from compliance POV. Hosted (global) can be used for US/APAC with routing rules that pin EU traffic to EU-only endpoints.

3) Throughput & concurrency:
- Baseline 120 req/s: multiple worker replicas across 3-4 GPUs in a dedicated pool will handle baseline with CPU egress bandwidth headroom.
- Peaks to 350 req/s: recommend autoscaling policy + burst capacity (pre-warmed) to absorb spikes; also use request-level queuing and backpressure for streaming sessions.
- Streaming concurrency (40 sessions): our streaming path supports chunked websocket responses; first-byte target <= 80ms is tight but achievable if you colocate session gateways near clients and pin models to low-latency instances.

4) Regional routing & failover:
- Smart routing policy: route by geo-ip + account tag; failover to secondary region only if configured (we can avoid cross-border failover for EU).
- Multi-region consistency: for session affinity we recommend a regional session token so subsequent requests stay in-region.

5) Data residency & logs:
- EU residency: data at rest and logs can be kept in EU-only storage when using Private/VPC or Dedicated EU clusters. Hosted global tenants will have cross-region replication disabled for EU-tagged traffic.
- Audit logs: we can provide 12mo retention; we need to walk through log volume to advise storage tiering (S3 lifecycle policies, archival).

6) Items I need from Finova to size accurately:
- 95/99 percentile prompt lengths and response token lengths
- % of requests that use streaming vs non-streaming
- expected geo split (US/EU/APAC % of traffic)

I'll attach a short readout (redwood-mrp-multipoint-routing.pdf) with recommended cluster sizes and autoscale configs. Happy to jump on a technical deep-dive next week to walk through network path and NAT/KMS options.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
